apps.description: The Academy's maintained build of KisMac: passive Wi-Fi scanning, hidden-SSID detection, client mapping, and GPS/KML export, remediated and rebuilt for macOS High Sierra. For network education and authorized testing of your own networks only. Installs as KisMac2.app under the Academy's own bundle identity (com.detroitautomationacademy.kismac) and carries the Academy audit entry. The bundle identity changed from the upstream com.igrsoft.kismac in this build, so the first launch is a fresh profile — preferences, Keychain items, and saved state do not carry over. It installs side by side with the Switchboard entry (Workbench.app).
apps.name: KisMac
apps.tagline: Wireless network discovery for education and authorized testing.

apps.description: The Academy's maintained build of Spectacle, the keyboard-driven window manager. The inherited Sparkle 1.22/DSA update channel is replaced under the Academy Update Infrastructure Standard (Sparkle 2.9.6, EdDSA, Academy appcast) at packaging. Release candidate: first Academy build — Academy bundle identity and the Academy audit entry verified in the shipped bundle. Named gap: the app icon is still the upstream color icon; the monochrome redraw is one design tranche in program order and blocks release, not this candidacy. Not yet run on the High Sierra rig. The bundled Sparkle updater stays at 1.22.0 in this candidate; the 2.9.6 + EdDSA step is a packaging-tranche decision.
apps.name: Spectacle
apps.tagline: Move and resize windows with the keyboard, maintained for High Sierra.

apps.description: The Academy's maintained build of MacDown. Uplift includes the Hoedown recursion-bound fix and the planned migration from legacy WebView to WKWebView; zero telemetry, MathJax bundled locally. Release candidate: first Academy build — Academy bundle identity and the Academy audit entry verified in the shipped bundle. Named gap: the app icon is still the upstream color icon; the monochrome redraw is one design tranche in program order and blocks release, not this candidacy. Not yet run on the High Sierra rig. Audit findings F-01/F-02/F-03/F-05/F-06 remain open.
apps.name: MacDown
apps.tagline: Markdown editor with live preview, maintained for High Sierra.

apps.description: The Academy's maintained build of Sequel Pro. Passwords stay in the macOS Keychain, as upstream correctly designed; the uplift addresses the MySQL 8 authentication gap left by the bundled MySQL 5.5-era client library. Release candidate: first Academy build — Academy bundle identity and the Academy audit entry verified in the shipped bundle. Named gap: the app icon is still the upstream color icon; the monochrome redraw is one design tranche in program order and blocks release, not this candidacy. Not yet run on the High Sierra rig. The bundled MySQL client library is 5.5.56 (end-of-life; the MariaDB swap is a later tranche).
apps.name: Sequel Pro
apps.tagline: MySQL database client, maintained for High Sierra.

apps.description: An Academy combine-fork: an Audacity-derived editor (pinned Audacity 3.7.9, the last line supporting macOS 10.13) with libVLC (pinned VLC 3.0.24) in a separate helper process for playback, conversion, and video-companion duties. Differentiators: High Sierra floor and a zero-telemetry build, verified by network capture before publication. Ships GPL-3.0 with full source, per the Gate 0 license record. Fork pending; sourceURL is set when the org repo is created.
apps.name: SoundDeck
apps.tagline: Audio editor with VLC-powered playback and conversion — in development.

apps.description: Staged internal build of the Academy's unified network utility (working name Switchboard), CI-built 2026-11-08; launched on the High Sierra rig 2026-11-08: the remediated KisMac discovery engine hosted in a new unified shell, a read-only AirPort base-station configuration view, Ping / Netstat / Traceroute / Speed Test diagnostics, and a local-only journal. Manage is read-only in this build — there is no configuration write path. The AirPort management pillar also ships as KisMac V2; Switchboard remains the umbrella product and the parity source of truth. Installs as Workbench.app under its own Academy bundle identity (com.detroitautomationacademy.workbench) and carries the Academy audit entry, distinct from KisMac — the two install side by side. (The earlier staged-v1-1 build shared the KisMac bundle identity and installing one replaced the other; corrected in staged-v1-2.) The Networks header now reads “Workbench” — staged-v1-4 is the surgical repair of the inherited “KisMac v0.3.4” header (ScanController), one line, nothing else changed.
apps.name: Switchboard
apps.tagline: One network utility: discovery, diagnostics, and read-only base-station view — staged test build.

apps.description: The Academy's native macOS edition of Live Transit Detroit: the whole regional network (DDOT, SMART, QLINE, People Mover) as one live map and vehicle list, rendered in native Core Graphics with no WebView or browser engine. Only the small live vehicle feed is fetched, on a conditional-GET refresh. Release candidate: live merged-network vehicles and alerts on the regional map; GTFS route polylines are not in this build yet. It carries the Academy audit entry and has not yet been launched on the High Sierra rig.
apps.name: Live Transit Detroit
apps.tagline: Live regional transit for the District of Detroit — native, no browser, built for High Sierra.

apps.description: Distro is the Detroit Automation Academy's native application-store app for macOS High Sierra: it browses the Academy catalog, downloads Academy-maintained apps from the AutomatedTechnologies GitHub org, verifies every download by SHA-256 before install, and carries no privileged helper. Prepared at DAADV3 T1 codification (2026-11-07); not yet published — publication remains gated on Distro tranche D-T5. Disassembled. Scanned. Recompiled. Distro distributes only apps carrying the Academy audit entry in their plist — proof of the Academy pipeline.
apps.name: Distro
apps.tagline: The Academy's application store for High Sierra — browse, install, and update Academy apps.

apps.description: The Academy's build of the open-source muse-desktop client (MIT, v0.3.0) on Electron 22.3.27 — the last Electron that runs on macOS 10.13 — so Intel High Sierra machines can run a Muse client at all; the official Muse app requires Apple Silicon and a current macOS. Packaged with the Academy monochrome icon. Unofficial build: not a Meta product and not endorsed by Meta. Unsigned test build. Runtime verified on the Academy's High Sierra rig: installed through Distro, it opens on first launch (2026-11-08). Its icon is cut to the amended SDS-3 construction — white tile and ink glyph, no black field.
apps.name: Muse (Academy Build)
apps.tagline: The Muse desktop client, rebuilt by the Academy for High Sierra.
